title: ops-stability-lab-90-day-canvas
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a working 90-day experiment canvas to align product, infra, serving runtime, and SRE on a focused reliability program that validates SLOs, operational runbooks, and error budget consumption practices for production inference routes. The goal is to run concrete experiments that produce actionable guardrails and a lightweight, cross-team playbook that we can ship into the console and runbook library.

High-level hypothesis:
If we run short, targeted reliability experiments (latency bucketing, transient-failure chaos, and prefix-cache hit drills) across 3 critical routes, then we will identify the top 3 contributors to SLO breaches, create mitigations that reduce breach frequency by >=40%, and produce a repeatable rollout checklist for feature teams.

Scope (what we will cover in 90 days):
- Routes: /generate (hosted), /chat (dedicated), /embeddings (private pilot).
- Signals: p50/p95/p99 latency, grpc open stream failures, model fallback rate, token-level cost delta, cache hit ratio, and error budget burn rate per route.
- Outputs: a short playbook (2–4 pages) per route, canary checklist, rollback triggers, SLO definition updates, and at least two engineered mitigations (one infra-level, one runtime-level).

Stakeholders and roles (working):
- Program lead (owner): Priya Kapoor — coordinates experiments, weekly syncs, compiles learning notes.
- SRE partners: Liam O'Neill, Chen Wei — run chaos drills, observe ops channels, implement monitoring alerts.
- Serving runtime: Ava Martinez — implements runtime flags (KV cache telemetry, batching knobs) and temporary patches for experiments.
- Product / Console: Diego Ramos — surfaces experiment dashboards in console and routes integration notes to product docs.
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success: ad-hoc support for private-deployment testbeds.

Week-by-week cadence (90 days, broken into 3 x 30-day sprints):
Sprint 0 (Week 0–2): prep and baseline
- Inventory: finalize route list, current SLOs, known bottlenecks. (Owner: Priya)
- Baseline metrics: collect two weeks of historical signals and produce baseline deck. (Owner: Liam)
- Quick-runbook draft: initial communication and on-call play notes for experiments. (Owner: Chen)
- Risk gating: identify any customer-impacting tenants and schedule maintenance windows. (Owner: Diego)
Sprint 1 (Week 3–5): probe and surface
- Latency bucketing experiment: push synthetic load with varying sequence lengths/contexts to map p95 sensitivity to seq length. (Owner: Ava)
- Cache-priming drills: measure KV cache warmup times across model variants. (Owner: Liam)
- Observability gap list: add missing traces/metrics and short-term dashboards. (Owner: Chen)
Sprint 2 (Week 6–9): targeted interventions
- Runtime knob tests: enable continuous batching heuristics and measure impact on p95 and cost. (Owner: Ava)
- Region-fallback run: simulate capacity constraints and validate smart routing/fallback policies. (Owner: Priya)
- Canary plan draft: definition of canary cohorts, traffic percentage, and rollback windows. (Owner: Diego)
Sprint 3 (Week 10–13): consolidate & ship
- Pilot mitigations in a dedicated pool for two routes. (Owners: runtime + infra)
- Update SLO definitions and error budget policies based on findings. (Owner: Liam)
- Final playbook + short exec summary and handoff to product/console. (Owner: Priya)

Success criteria (binary + numeric):
- Binary: playbook exists and is accepted by product and SRE leads.
- Numeric: prototype mitigations reduce p95 breach events by >=40% across the tested routes during piloted windows.
- Numeric: error budget burn rate per route shows 25% lower variance week-over-week for 4 consecutive weeks post-intervention.

Experiment designs (short forms):
1) Latency bucketing matrix
- Variables: sequence length bins (0–64, 65–256, 257–1024), model variant (full, quantized), batch size settings (1, 4, 8).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99, kv-cache hit ratio, token generation time.
- Quick win: if p95 increases >2x for seq length bin, produce a routing policy suggestion to split requests by expected length.

2) Error-budget treadmill (simulated partial outages)
- Simulate intermittent GPU worker loss in dedicated pool (10%–30% short spikes) and observe error budget consumption under existing fallback policies.
- Validate that automatic fallback to lighter model variants triggers and does not exceed customer-configured fidelity thresholds.
- Rollback trigger: if customer request error rate >1% for >10 minutes, cancel experiment and enact immediate rollback.

3) Cache warmup & priming test
- Run prefix-heavy synthetic workload to estimate time-to-warm for KV cache per model.
- Measure cold-start p95 and track reduction after pre-warming step.
- If warmup reduces p95 breaches by >=30% for short-tail traffic, add pre-warm recommendation to onboarding docs.

Operational runbook sketch (to be converted to canonical template):
- Pre-experiment checklist: announce to slack, confirm maintenance window, create JIRA with automation link, ensure backup model pinned, enable tighter alerting.
- During experiment: minute-level updates in #sre-stability-lab, one on-call rotation assigned, rapid rollback owner declared.
- Post-experiment: debrief with evidence artifacts (dashboards + logs), action items tagged in JIRA, update console text for affected routes.

Communication plan:
- Weekly sync (30 minutes) with stakeholders; pre-read deck by Monday morning.
- Tacticals in #sre-stability-lab channel; incident-like cadence if rollback triggers.
- Exec summary at program close: 1-page top findings, 1 slide per mitigation (cost/latency/ops impact).

Open questions / risks:
- Customer-facing thresholds: do product teams want strict 99.9% availability per route or more lenient values for experimental windows? (assigned to Diego)
- Telemetry gaps: we lack tokenized latencies for the embeddings route in private pilot; need a short instrumentation spike. (assigned to Chen)
- Resource contention: dedicated pool experiments may interfere with other tenants; require coordinated maintenance windows and quota reservations.

Quick decision log (work-in-progress):
- 2025-11-03: Decided to include /embeddings pilot despite weaker telemetry — will instrument and run a shorter experiment. (Priya)
- 2025-11-05: Agreed on rollback threshold for error-budget treadmill: 1% request errors sustained for 10 minutes. (Liam, Chen)

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Finish baseline deck and share with stakeholders (Priya, due: 2025-11-07).
- Create JIRA SRE-482 and link runbook template (Liam).
- Implement lightweight KV cache telemetry on embeddings cluster (Ava).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep experiments small and observable. No heavy-handed infra changes unless we have clear rollback.
- Emphasize automated evidence capture (dashboards, traces) — manual screenshots won't cut it for handoffs.

Appendix: short list of dashboards to create
- Route overview: p50/p95/p99 by model variant and region (time-series + heatmap).
- Error budget burn: rolling 1h and 24h burn rates with annotations for experiments.
- Fallback activation timeline: traces showing when fallback policy ran and subsequent success/failure.

References / quick links (work-in-progress):
- Runtime flags doc: GH PR 1243
- Existing SLO catalog: Confluence OPS-STABILITY-LAB-2025
- Past incident notes: slack thread ts 170942*** (internal)

End of canvas — leave comments below or add to the JIRA linked_artifacts.
